evidence.claim: There is NO kNN candidate graph. For each frame pair the transformer scores the DENSE n_src x n_tgt matrix, then probs = softmax(raw, dim=0), which normalises over all sources for each target, with no null or no-parent column. Only pairs with probs > cfg.threshold are written as candidate edges. So the 'edge_prob 0' pairs WERE scored; their probability was simply thrown away.
evidence.source: tools/repo/scripts/predict_unet_transformer.py lines 449-491 (predict_edges -> softmax dim=0 -> if probs[i, j] > cfg.threshold)

evidence.claim: exp39 sets the candidate threshold to 0.48 (BIOHUB_DUAL_SEED_EDGE_THRESHOLD; the patch sets cfg.threshold = edge_candidate_threshold). The secondary-seed blend and the bidirectional harmonic blend (forward softmax over dim=1) happen INSIDE predict_edges, so the probs seen at the threshold loop are already the final blended values. A sidecar dump at that loop therefore captures the shipped probabilities.
evidence.source: experiments/exp39_sjlee947_tight55_divnetveto/exp39-sjlee947-tight55-divnetveto.ipynb, raw line 216 (env) and raw line 246 (patched predictor: primary/secondary softmax dim=0, forward_prob softmax dim=1, cfg.threshold override)

evidence.claim: Relink cost = motion + 0.05*raw - BONUS*prob with BONUS = 1.0 in exp39. learned_edge_probs is built from the post-ILP edge list, so any pair outside it gets 0.0 through .get(key, 0.0). Because p < 0.48 for every missing pair, restoring them changes a cost by less than 0.48 um. That only flips near-ties, not the 9.4 um swap geometry.

The tracksdata ILP solver returns only the solution subgraph by default (return_solution=True). Candidates at >= 0.48 that the ILP did not select are therefore also missing from learned_edge_probs, not only the sub-threshold pairs.

Trackastra keeps predicted associations down to a low threshold (alpha = 0.05) for its downstream linker. It uses a 'parental quiet softmax' (exp / (1 + sum)), which gives an implicit null option, and a spatial distance mask. This is precedent for passing low-probability pair scores to the linker, not only the argmax.

The transformer (and the UNet features, through the joint edge loss) trained on GT nodes with GT coordinates only, on all 199 train videos. So a fold retrain started 'from the public init' is NOT out-of-fold: the init has already seen every held-out video. An honest OOF score needs the UNet and the transformer retrained from scratch per leak-group fold, which does not fit in 2 days and ~20 GPU hours (GUESS, based on B34's 3-4 day estimate for only 2 folds).
evidence.source: tools/repo/scripts/train_unet_transformer.py, simple_node_transformer.py; CONTEXT.md lines 1178-1180 (B34 audit: trains on GT-node pairs, Kaggle-only paths, no resume, not an honest LOEO)

evidence.claim: In-sample base predictions bias second-level models and thresholds tuned on them. This is the standard reason for OOF stacking, and it supports the concern in principle.
evidence.source: Kaggle discussion general/18793 (stacking/OOF); arXiv 2206.08473; KDnuggets stacking guide

evidence.claim: The project already decided that probe 29 (edge filter, pending) answers the 'is ef in-sample?' question directly on unseen embryos. An OOF audit adds no decision value for probe 29 and costs about 1 day of trainer work plus GPU time.
evidence.source: CONTEXT.md 2026-09-24 13:25 UTC note ('probe 29 answers the transfer question directly')

evidence.claim: Swap and u_diverted FN are node-position errors (matched endpoints 4.4/4.7 um from GT vs 1.8 um; the motion model prefers our link in 98.6% of cases; 2x2 re-assignment = -0.00004). Better pair probabilities cannot fix them, which limits the plumbing upside to the 'ILP both none' and zero-prob in-edge pockets (about 450 TP / 340 FP evaluable).
A related public fine-tune of the edge transformer, with impostor duplicate nodes as hard negatives (lr 2e-5, 6-8 epochs), exists but reports no LB number.

implementation_notes:
FACTS FROM CODE. (1) The pair scores are dense: every source x target pair of each frame pair gets a value. The candidate set is simply {p > 0.48}, with max_parents/max_children caps applied greedily. (2) softmax(dim=0) normalises over SOURCES for each target, so a target sitting between two of our tracks (the duplicate / swap situation) splits its mass, e.g. 0.45 / 0.45, and BOTH pairs fall below 0.48 and are lost. That is the one case where restoring sub-threshold probabilities carries real information. (3) The exp39 patch overrides cfg.threshold and blends primary/secondary seeds plus a bidirectional harmonic inside predict_edges, so hook AFTER blending: at the 'for i..for j if probs[i,j] > cfg.threshold' loop, or better, vectorised with np.argwhere(probs >= 0.05). Keep the ILP input unchanged (threshold stays 0.48). (4) The relink bonus is 1.0 um per unit of prob; sub-threshold additions are worth at most 0.48 um.
PITFALLS. (a) edge['edge_prob'] is also used by the edge filter (the rule tests p == 0, i.e. 'unscored') and by short-track rescue (mean edge prob threshold 0.82-0.88). Put the sidecar probability in a SEPARATE field (relink_prob), and keep ef keyed on ILP membership (an 'ilp_member' flag), not on prob == 0. Otherwise probe 29's rule silently changes. (b) Node-id mapping: the predictor's gi indexes the concatenated coords array. Whether tracksdata/geff node ids equal gi is a GUESS; join on (t, z, y, x) integer coords instead and assert a 100% match. If exp51 float coordinates ship, the join key must be the pre-refinement integer peak. (c) Dense matrices reach 2,600 x 2,600 per frame pair. Store only p >= 0.05 (Trackastra's alpha) as float16 in a per-video parquet: about 1-3 entries per target, so a few MB per video (GUESS). (d) The OOF retrain as proposed ('5 folds from the public init') is not out-of-fold (the init saw all 199 videos, and the UNet features got the edge-loss gradient on all 199). Drop it. Use probe 29's LB delta vs probe 28 as the transfer audit for ef, and keep relink-off-style decisions on the LB (they already are). (e) The lab cache (friend A) almost certainly lacks sub-threshold probabilities (GUESS, check its schema: if it holds only geff edges, a GPU re-dump is mandatory).
WHAT DOES NOT WORK AS STATED: the 'kNN candidate graph' premise (it is dense), the 'network only scored ILP pairs' premise (it scored all pairs), and the OOF-from-init plan.
refined_change: Drop the OOF retrain entirely. Keep only the plumbing fix, re-framed. In the inference notebook, record the blended per-target softmax probabilities for all pairs with p >= 0.05 (sidecar dict keyed by node pair) at the existing threshold loop, leaving the ILP candidates (p > 0.48) unchanged. In filter_output_graph, build relink_probs = max(ILP-edge prob, sidecar prob) and pass THAT to motion_relink_edges, so pairs the network scored but the ILP did not keep get their real bonus instead of 0. Keep edge['edge_prob'] and the edge-filter rule keyed on ILP membership (new ilp_member flag), so probe 29/30 semantics are preserved. Variants: BONUS 1.0 (as shipped) and 1.5. Optional later variant (only if the first wins): let the edge filter re-link an orphaned target to its best sidecar source (p >= 0.2) instead of only the ILP's free alternative.
refined_lab_test: GPU step (required; the CPU lab cannot produce these probabilities): one Kaggle 2xT4 run of the exp48 inference code with the sidecar hook on the 64 SELECTION 6bba videos (plus the 71 44b6 confirmation videos if time allows). Ideally piggy-back on the exp51/V1284 capture pass so the UNet runs once. Output per video: nodes (t, z, y, x integer, pre-refinement) and a pairs parquet (t, src_idx, tgt_idx, p_blend float16, p >= 0.05). Sanity checks before any scoring: (i) node coordinates match the lab cache 100%; (ii) the set {p > 0.48} after caps reproduces the cached ILP candidate edges exactly (tolerance 0 edges). If either check fails, stop: the cache is not the same pipeline. CPU lab (Kaggle CPU kernel): exp48 + ef + stitch control vs the same + relink_probs from the sidecar at BONUS 1.0 and 1.5, on SELECTION, then one CONFIRMATION run for the best variant. Standard gate: >= +0.002, each embryo >= +0.001, win rate >= 55% per embryo, 90% CI lower bound > 0. Diagnostics to report: the number of final edges whose relink choice changed; TP/FP among the changed evaluable edges; the delta restricted to the 'ILP both none' and 'u_diverted zero-prob in-edge' pockets. In-sample audit: replace the OOF AUC comparison with probe 29's public delta. If LB(29) - LB(28) < 0.3 x the local ef delta (+0.016), treat ef-derived thresholds as in-sample and stop tuning on network probabilities. No retraining.
expected_gain: Plumbing: +0.000 to +0.001 local (GUESS). The pockets hold about 450 TP / 340 FP evaluable, the bonus can move costs by at most 0.48 um, and the large swap/diverted FN class is node-position error that probabilities cannot fix. Public likely similar or smaller. The OOF retrain has no score value and its decision value is already supplied by probe 29. Priority: LOW. Run it only as a free add-on to a GPU capture pass that happens anyway (exp51/V1284); do not spend a dedicated GPU run or an LB probe on it alone.
